chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When the fasting person vomits, he has broken his fast; and if it reaches him (by force) without him vomiting, let him complete his fast."
ai.seo_question: Does voluntary vomiting break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between voluntary and involuntary vomiting regarding the validity of the fast, a key topic in Shia fiqh. The term 'reaching by force' (idhra') implies an external cause or natural occurrence, distinguishing it from self-induced vomiting which breaks the fast. This ruling underscores the principle of ease in fasting, ensuring that unintentional acts do not invalidate the worship.
